messages:
alice_sales: Heads-up: Prospect (FinCo) hit a hard failure during prep for tomorrows demo. They POST a single JSON payload ~1.1MB -> gateway returns 413. Demo blocked. Need quick options they can do without changing corp infra.
mark_se: Thanks. 413 points to a proxy/nginx/APIM body limit before our gateway. Do we have their exact response headers or error body?
alice_sales: Customer pasted the APIM error: "413 Request Entity Too Large - The request size exceeds the configured limit." No stack from their side. They say payload is UTF-8 JSON, includes a ~300k CSV as a string field plus chat history.
tina_ml: Quick checklist: are they base64-encoding attachments? base64 increases size ~33%. If it's raw CSV as plain text, gzipping client-side usually helps a lot.
jane_se: If they can't change APIM, options ranked: (A) Stream via websocket to our streaming endpoint (small frames, bypass single-body limit), (B) client chunking + reassembly endpoint, (C) host file on accessible object store + reference URL in request. Which are feasible?
alice_sales: They said presigned S3 is blocked by corporate policy. They can do websocket or chunking but want examples and cost implications.
mark_se: Websocket is easiest for demo: open a persistent connection, send smaller messages with parts of the context, we assemble server-side. This avoids a single big POST. We can issue a short-lived streaming key. Sam, can you create one?
sam_support: Yes I can create a demo streaming key + temporary endpoint. Need their egress IP(s) to allowlist. Also confirm they can speak TLS w/ websockets.
ina_support: (automated) Note: streaming keys are rate-limited to demo-level throughput.
tina_ml: Client guidance for chunking: split into logical sections (metadata, CSV rows, convo blocks). Aim for chunks <=180k bytes. For token estimation: rough heuristic 1 token ~= 4 chars for english text, or compute using their tokenizer. Provide snippet.
jane_se: Also encourage them to replace the CSV with an embeddings vector if the use-case is retrieval/semantic search. That reduces tokens massively and lowers cost. If they need raw rows for model synthesis, chunk & summarize older rows into compressed summaries.
alice_sales: Pricing question: they asked if chunking/streaming increases cost.
mark_se: Cost = sum(input tokens + output tokens. Streaming vs single POST doesn't change billing, but sending raw CSV as tokens obviously costs more vs sending embeddings or summaries. We can run a quick estimate once they share sample payload.
sam_support: Created support ticket S-8804 and a streaming token with 4-hour TTL. Included connection info and IP allowlist request.
jane_se: For immediate demo, suggest this runbook: 1) Try websocket demo token we issued. 2) If they can't websocket, implement client gzip and chunk <=180k then call /v1/assemble with ordered parts. We have sample python+curl in the KB I can paste.
tina_ml: Adding the python chunker snippet to S-8804 now (short). Also: if they gzip, set Content-Encoding: gzip. Note: some proxies count compressed length; confirm with their APIM team.
mark_se: Edge case: if they reassemble > model window, requests will be truncated by model. Recommend they pick model variant with larger context or pre-filter to important segments.
alice_sales: Perfect. I'll relay streaming token and ask for sample payload for cost estimate. Can someone jump on a 15-min call?
sam_support: I'm available in 15. I'll include alice in the ticket email.
jane_se: If this moves to a longer pilot and they need single-file uploads, propose Dedicated with custom gateway; pricing and SLA addendum needed. I can draft a rough quote.
alice_sales: Thanks team. Will update prospect and loop back. :thumbsup:
